definition: Dr.Fill is a computer program that solves American-style crossword puzzles.
details: It was developed by Matt Ginsberg, who described it in the Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research. Ginsberg claims in that article that Dr.Fill is among the top fifty crossword solvers in the world.

explainer.lead: Dr.Fill is a computer program built to solve American-style crossword puzzles. Developed by Matt Ginsberg, it turns the familiar challenge of clues and crossing answers into a task for artificial intelligence.

tiers.eli5: Dr.Fill is a computer program that tries to finish crosswords. It is a bit like a puzzle partner who thinks of possible answers and checks whether their letters fit with the words crossing them. Its creator says it can solve puzzles as well as some of the world's best human crossword players.
tiers.practitioner: Dr.Fill is a specialized solver for American-style crossword instances, not a general-purpose language system. An evaluation would provide a grid and its clues, then assess the completed entries against the puzzle solution. Results should not be generalized to other puzzle formats, and Ginsberg's top-fifty statement should be treated as his claim rather than an established benchmark ranking.
tiers.paperLevel: Dr.Fill maps an American-style crossword instance, consisting of a grid and clues, to a completed crossword solution. Matt Ginsberg described the program in the Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research and claimed that it ranks among the world's top fifty crossword solvers. Its stated problem scope is American-style crosswords.

explainer.example: Suppose the clue “Feline pet (3)” suggests CAT, while a crossing answer requires the pattern C_T. CAT fits both the clue and the crossing constraint, so it can occupy that three-letter slot; an entry such as CAP would fail the feline clue even though it fits the letters.

usedIn.name: American-style crossword solving

explainer.intuition: A crossword is more than a set of isolated questions: every answer must also agree with the letters of the answers crossing it. Dr.Fill applies computing to that combined challenge of interpreting clues and fitting entries into one grid.
howItWorks: Take an American-style crossword grid and its clues as the puzzle to solve.
Work out possible entries for the clue-and-slot combinations.
Use the grid's shared letters to check whether crossing entries agree.
Produce a completed crossword as the solution.
explainer.whyItMatters: Dr.Fill shows how an AI system can tackle a pastime that combines clue interpretation with tightly connected letter constraints. Ginsberg's top-fifty claim also frames crossword solving as a comparison between a program and skilled human solvers.
misconceptions: Dr.Fill is a program, not a person or a general-purpose chatbot.
The top-fifty ranking is Ginsberg's claim, not a separately established result.
Solving American-style crosswords does not by itself demonstrate general human-level understanding.
